quest.title: So-Called Work
quest.description: After having made one mistake too many at work, Linling is in danger of losing her job...
quest.rewards_formatted: Linling's Anthology of Selected Poetry x1

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: I'm finished, it's all over for me this time...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: *sobs* Nervous An said that I might not be cut out for this line of work...

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: Isn't he just firing me? What do I do? I... I'm always working so hard...

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: Well... Didn't I ask you before to help me count boats?

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: I trusted in your ability, so I didn't double check the data you gave me, and handed it in directly.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: A lot of the numbers turned out to be wrong... Nervous An really lost his temper.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: Won't you help me talk to him? I—I'll do my job seriously from now on! And I won't call on you to help me out again, either!

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: But I dare not go to ask him myself...

choices.text: Were the previous boat tallies wrong?

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: Yes! Didn't I ask you to help me out with them before?

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: I trusted in your ability, so I didn't double check the data. I handed it in directly... and a lot of it turned out to be wrong.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: But I only asked for your help from time to time. I also tallied a great deal of numbers myself...

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: So when put side by side, I didn't know where I had gone wrong at all, which made Nervous An lose his temper...

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: Please help me talk to him! I—I'll do my job seriously from now on! And I won't ask you to help me out again, either!

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: But I dare not go to ask him myself...

dialogues.speaker: Nervous An
dialogues.text: *sigh* Really, this is...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can we talk about Linling?

dialogues.speaker: Nervous An
dialogues.text: Hmm? You're asking about Linling? Well... How do I say this? She's just not really suited for her job.

dialogues.speaker: Nervous An
dialogues.text: Specifically, the mistakes she's made in her data entry are far too egregious.

dialogues.speaker: Nervous An
dialogues.text: As for this week's data, only one or two days out of seven have the correct numbers. Even a purely visual inspection would be more accurate.

dialogues.speaker: Nervous An
dialogues.text: How can I leave this job to her with that attitude?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, if it's just numbers...

dialogues.speaker: Nervous An
dialogues.text: There is no "just" when it comes to work.

dialogues.speaker: Nervous An
dialogues.text: If a single plank in a wooden barrel is a little short, then the volume of the whole barrel goes down.

dialogues.speaker: Nervous An
dialogues.text: It is the same with work. If we get careless about even one matter, we will drag the larger work through the mud.

dialogues.speaker: Nervous An
dialogues.text: Let's take tallying up the number of boats, for example. If the numbers are not accurate, then the various activities we conduct at the harbor will also be imprecise.

dialogues.speaker: Nervous An
dialogues.text: Imprecision there can be costly, and even if someone remedies the issue, the time unnecessarily lost fixing the problem cannot be gained back.

dialogues.speaker: Nervous An
dialogues.text: Do you understand now?

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: Still, we do lack manpower here at the harbor, so I most likely won't fire her.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: How should I put it... "a plank shorter" is better than "a plank short," no?

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: The person in charge of reviewing cargo is unable to be here due to an emergency. Tell Linling that her help there will be expedient.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: If nothing serious goes wrong with her work there, then she can return to her job tallying boats when the person in charge of the review returns to work.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: Hmm... I guess this can be considered a test, and something of a second chance.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: Give this manifest to Linling. Ask her to conduct checks according to it, and make markings on the back once each check is completed.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: Also, please tell her to pull her socks up. If she slips up here as well, then there won't be any more second chances.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: What will you tell her? That she's fired? No, she's not fired just yet.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: We have a dire lack of manpower here at the harbor. How do I say this... "a plank shorter" is still better than "a plank short," yes?

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: The person in charge of reviewing cargo is unable to be here due to an emergency. Tell Linling that her help there will be expedient.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: If nothing serious goes wrong with her work there, then she can return to her job tallying boats when the person in charge of the review returns to work.

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: Oh, what shall I do about work...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nervous An says he's giving you another chance.

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: Really! Wonderful! That's great!

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: Eh? A cargo review? Oh no... I've never done that before...

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: If I make another mistake, I'm definitely finished. No, I have to make preparations first...

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: I need to find the previous review standards, and also the previous standard formats...

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: Could you help me confirm the amount of cargo first? You just need to check the cargo numbers against the document and see if they're accurate. I will conduct a more detailed review later.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: Thank you so much. I'll be making preparations here in the meantime.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: I can't mess up this time...

choices.text: You can leave everything to us.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: No, I can't, not this time. A cargo review is way more complex than tallying boats. I have to do this myself.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: So, please just confirm the amounts of cargo. I will do a more specific review afterwards.

talks.objective: Review the goods on board the ship

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: Have you ascertained the numbers?

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: Great. My preparations are almost complete as well. I will review all those goods once again in a while.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: Oh, right! Please take this as thanks for your help. I will go and review the cargo in a moment. This time, nothing can be allowed to go wrong...

choices.text: You weren't writing poetry, were you?

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: Of course not! I do have a sense of priorities, you know. This isn't the time to be writing poetry...

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: ...I can't write poetry at work anymore. I've got to focus...

choices.text: Work comes first in the end.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: I know that. But doing the same thing day in, day out, year on year... you eventually get bored, you know?

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: And, well, it's precisely because it's this kind of sideline job, you know? It's not that important, and no one really pays you mind, so you start to drift off after a while...

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: Nervous An always says things like "every job is important" and "every job is decisive..."

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: But if that's the case, why's everyone still so picky about the kind of work they want to do?

choices.text: You need to take responsibility for your work.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: I only ask for your help occasionally. I do it myself most of the time.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: I know I should take responsibility for my work. But the busier it gets, the more I feel like slacking off. That's why I ask for your help at times.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: If I really were to become idle, I find myself looking for things to do instead...

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: Well, you haven't worked a day in your life, have you? There's no use telling you all this...

choices.text: Why do you want to write poetry so much?

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: Why are you suddenly asking me this? Let me think... Well, why do you think a person works?

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: The way I see it, "working for the sake of continuing to work" is a little too boring.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: How I say this? Everyone has got to have their dreams, right? A dream that's totally separate from the daily drudgery of work.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: That way, even in moments when you're so tired that you think you might break, you can take refuge in your dreams.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: But this is just my way of thinking, of course. I have no idea how adventurers would think of this problem.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: When I look at the way they do nothing but live for their dreams, I feel like I need some kind of daily work to ground myself instead.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: Still... Hahaha, take it from me: dreams are just dreams. When you work, you still need to keep your feet firmly planted.

dialogues.speaker: Nervous An
dialogues.text: I'm a cooper: I'm neither particularly good with my hands, nor do I have any particular talents.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: Well, that is to say that I'm like someone who repairs barrels, and who needs a single plank of wood to finish my wooden barrel.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: But the plank I have in hand isn't of good quality. It's just a little short, and if I use it to make my wooden barrel, its capacity is going to be lowered significantly.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: Still, if I want to get a new plank, who knows when I will finish that barrel.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: And given that the deadline for finishing the barrel is drawing near, I have to choose the lesser of two evils.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: Who knows how many people there are under the sun who are coopers like me, who are facing a dilemma similar to mine.

choices.text: Can we talk about Linling's job?

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: Her job? Ah, yes. She did ask you to help her tally boat numbers in the past, didn't she? I know about that.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: Don't look so surprised. As long as we get results, I'm really not picky as to how she does her work.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: Besides, the rewards she gives you are taken out of her own pocket.

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: But as for her reporting data without reviewing it first...

response.speaker: Nervous An
response.text: That irresponsible attitude is what really made me angry.

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: Reviewing cargo is much more of a hassle than tallying boats.

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: This time, I have to be very careful. I can't make a single mistake...
